invariant: Versions are positive, unique, and contiguous from one.
lifecycle: Appended once by the migration runner immediately before its migration commits; never updated or deleted.
justification: The migration ledger exists before representative-v1 and is schema provenance rather than scenario data.

invariant: The name exactly matches the versioned migration filename recorded by the runner.
lifecycle: Appended once with its migration and immutable thereafter.
justification: The migration runner owns the applied-script identity; a fixture must not manufacture ledger rows.

invariant: The 32-byte digest equals the SHA-256 of the exact applied migration file.
lifecycle: Computed before execution, recorded in the same migration transaction, and immutable thereafter.
justification: The digest authenticates migration history and cannot be derived from representative scenario content.

invariant: The timestamp records when the migration ledger row was inserted by the database.
lifecycle: Assigned once by the database default during migration and immutable thereafter.
justification: Wall-clock migration time predates and is independent of representative-v1.

invariant: The value records the PostgreSQL role that applied the migration.
lifecycle: Captured once from current_user during migration and immutable thereafter.
justification: The applying role is deployment provenance, not fixture-controlled identity data.

invariant: The value records the server version that executed the migration.
lifecycle: Captured once from server_version during migration and immutable thereafter.
justification: The PostgreSQL runtime version is environment provenance and must not be forged by a seed.

invariant: A successful or reconciled call has no error code; a terminal failed call records a sanitized provider or transport discriminator rather than secret-bearing text.
lifecycle: Starts NULL and remains NULL through the successful representative-v1 lifecycle; a failure adapter sets it when recording a failed terminal response and it is retained for audit.
justification: Representative-v1 intentionally covers a successful reconciled call, so inventing an error code would contradict that lifecycle; failure-code vocabulary belongs to a dedicated failure scenario.
